raw_response:
I have farmed this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil, I know what it needs, and I know what pays.

The wheat-maize rotation is what I will do again this year. It has always been the backbone here on the North China Plain, and at 73 I am not going to gamble on something unfamiliar. My son helps during the busy periods, but I manage the decisions and most of the lighter work myself.

I farm 8 mu. That is the right size for me now. I tried 15 mu in my sixties and it wore me down.

**Wheat (winter):** I will plant improved wheat — Kenong 199, which has done well on my plot the last several years. Good resistance to stripe rust, stable yield. I will rotary till before planting to work in the base fertilizer. I have cut my irrigation to three times: pre-winter water to help establishment, jointing water, and heading water. I was watering four times ten years ago, but the well depth has nearly doubled since I was young. Everyone here knows the aquifer is in trouble. Three waterings is enough if timed right. I will apply two rounds of pesticide — one fungicide in spring for powdery mildew and one combined spray at heading.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed hybrid maize into the stubble — no tillage. Saves my back, saves moisture, saves diesel. I use Zhengdan 958, reliable and widely available. Maize gets the summer rain mostly, so I irrigate only once if the rains are late at establishment. One pesticide application for corn borer, mid-season.

I keep nitrogen modest. I have seen neighbors pile it on and watch it wash away or lock up. My yields are not the highest in the village, but my input costs are low and my soil has not turned sour.

Irrigation is deliberately reduced to three applications for wheat and one for maize, reflecting decades of observed groundwater decline in Hebei and alignment with provincial water-saving policy. No-tillage direct seeding for maize reduces labor demand appropriate to the farmer's age and preserves soil moisture after wheat harvest.
